observations: Not a failure, a wording risk for the reviewer: docs/kubernetes.md and skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md both say '/usr/local/bin, /opt and /home are read-only'. /home itself is root-owned and refuses a write, as measured, but the role's own $HOME (/home/legion, drwx------ legion legion) is writable — a role reading that sentence could conclude its home is read-only. The sentence's own evidence block (id, then the apt refusal) is accurate and is what carries the argument.

The psql justification is exact only with an external database: packages/dispatch/e2e/local-instance.ts:119 requires go, psql, flock and openssl always, and docker as well when DATABASE_URL is unset — and no Legion pod has docker. All four of the always-required tools are in the image (openssl and flock already were), so a role that brings its own DATABASE_URL can now start that suite; a role without one still cannot, for want of docker, not for want of psql. Neither document claims otherwise.

One negative control of mine was void and is not relied on: psql with a wrong PGPASSWORD still succeeded against the sidecar, because the postgres image trusts host connections by default — so the authentication path was not exercised. The refused-connection control and the masked-PATH probe refusal stand in its place.
